_note: SECTION 13 NEIGHBOURHOODS. Geographic, lifestyle and landmark descriptions below are general, publicly-known facts about real communities in Markham and the surrounding GTA, written originally for this site. Market statistics are deliberately null: average price, median price, days on market and sale-to-list ratio require a licensed TRREB data source and must never be estimated. Kaylin's commentary fields are empty and awaiting her own words.

neighbourhoods.name: Unionville
neighbourhoods.tagline: A preserved 19th-century main street inside a modern city.
neighbourhoods.intro: Unionville is one of the oldest settled areas in Markham, built around a Main Street that has kept its 19th-century storefronts while the surrounding city grew into one of the largest employment centres in the GTA. It is a rare combination: a genuine heritage core, strong schools, and immediate access to Highway 407.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Main Street Unionville runs from Highway 7 north to Toogood Pond, lined with independent restaurants, cafes and small retail in restored heritage buildings. Weekends draw people from across the region, which is part of the appeal and part of the trade-off.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Housing stock ranges from protected heritage homes on and around Main Street to large detached homes in the surrounding subdivisions and newer condominium development along Highway 7.
transportation: GO Transit Stouffville line, Unionville GO Station
Viva and YRT bus service along Highway 7
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. School catchments change; verify current boundaries directly with the school board before relying on them.

neighbourhoods.name: Cornell
neighbourhoods.tagline: New urbanism, built to a plan.
neighbourhoods.intro: Cornell was master-planned on new urbanist principles: narrow lots, front porches close to the sidewalk, rear laneway garages, and a street grid designed to be walked rather than driven. It is one of the clearest examples of the approach anywhere in Ontario.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: The neighbourhood is anchored by Cornell Community Centre and Library and by Markham Stouffville Hospital. The design intent shows in daily life: short blocks, visible front doors, and a community centre placed within walking distance of most of the plan.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Predominantly newer construction. Laneway-garage homes are common, which changes both streetscape and parking from a conventional subdivision.
transportation: Cornell Bus Terminal, YRT and Viva
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Markham Village
neighbourhoods.tagline: The original town, still legible in the street pattern.
neighbourhoods.intro: Markham Village is the historic core the wider city takes its name from. Main Street Markham North still carries the original commercial frontage, and the surrounding blocks hold some of the oldest residential stock in York Region alongside decades of later infill.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Quieter than Unionville and more residential in character. Independent businesses, long-standing community events, and mature tree cover on the older streets.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Unusually wide range of construction eras on adjacent streets, from 19th-century century homes to postwar bungalows to recent infill. Lot sizes vary considerably block to block.
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Berczy Village
neighbourhoods.intro: Berczy Village is a largely late-1990s-to-2000s community in north-central Markham that has developed a strong reputation with families, driven substantially by its schools and by a consistent housing stock of detached and townhome product.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Suburban in form and quiet in character, with retail concentrated at the plazas along Major Mackenzie Drive and Kennedy Road rather than in a walkable main street.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Consistent construction era means comparables are relatively clean, which matters when pricing a sale here.
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Catchment reputation is frequently cited in this area; confirm current boundaries with the board rather than relying on listings.

neighbourhoods.name: Angus Glen
neighbourhoods.tagline: Large lots on the edge of the golf course.
neighbourhoods.intro: Angus Glen developed around the golf club of the same name in north Markham. It holds some of the larger detached housing stock in the city, and the community centre is among the most substantial municipal facilities in York Region.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Low density by Markham standards, with wide streets and a strong association with the golf club and the community centre.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Lot frontage and finish level vary widely, which makes comparable selection genuinely difficult here. This is a neighbourhood where pricing by square footage alone tends to mislead.
landmarks: Angus Glen Community Centre and Library
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Cathedraltown
neighbourhoods.tagline: Built around a cathedral, on a formal plan.
neighbourhoods.intro: Cathedraltown is organised around the Cathedral of the Transfiguration, with a formal street plan and a densely built mix of detached homes, towns and low-rise condominium buildings. It is one of the more architecturally distinctive plans in Markham.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Compact and walkable within its own boundaries, with the cathedral as an unmistakable visual anchor.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Higher density than most Markham subdivisions, with a correspondingly wider range of price points in a small area.
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Wismer Commons
neighbourhoods.tagline: Consistent stock, strong demand, tight comparables.
neighbourhoods.intro: Wismer Commons is a 2000s-era community in north Markham with a housing stock that is unusually consistent in age and type. It draws steady family demand and sits close to the Mount Joy GO Station.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Residential and quiet, with retail along Bur Oak and Markham Road and green space threaded through the plan.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: The consistency of the stock cuts both ways: comparables are clean, but standing out as a seller requires deliberate preparation and presentation.
transportation: Mount Joy GO Station, Stouffville line
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Thornhill
neighbourhoods.tagline: An older community split across two municipalities.
neighbourhoods.intro: Thornhill straddles the boundary between Markham and Vaughan, following Yonge Street north of Steeles. It is one of the older communities in the region, with a heritage conservation district at its centre and mature, established residential streets around it.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: More urban in feel than most of Markham, with the Yonge Street corridor providing continuous retail and transit and easy access south into Toronto.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Because Thornhill spans two municipalities, taxes, services and by-laws differ depending on which side of the boundary a property sits. Confirm the municipality before making assumptions.
transportation: Viva Blue and YRT along Yonge Street
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Greensborough
neighbourhoods.tagline: Newer construction, next to the GO line.
neighbourhoods.intro: Greensborough is a newer community in northeast Markham, built largely in the 2000s and 2010s, with the Mount Joy GO Station on its edge and a mix of detached, town and condominium product.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Suburban and family-oriented, with the Greensborough Community Centre and a network of trails through the plan.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Proximity to Mount Joy GO is a genuine pricing factor here and worth isolating when selecting comparables.
transportation: Mount Joy GO Station, Stouffville line
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Milliken Mills
neighbourhoods.tagline: South Markham, at the Toronto boundary.
neighbourhoods.intro: Milliken Mills sits in south Markham against the Steeles Avenue boundary with Toronto. It is one of the more established parts of the city, with significant retail and employment along the Steeles and Kennedy corridors.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Dense and well-serviced, with major retail centres, extensive dining, and the shortest drive into Scarborough and North York of any Markham community.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Largely 1970s through 1990s construction. Lot sizes are often larger than newer north Markham subdivisions at comparable price points.
transportation: YRT and TTC connection at Steeles
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Richmond Hill
neighbourhoods.intro: Richmond Hill sits immediately west of Markham, organised along Yonge Street with the Oak Ridges Moraine at its northern edge. It offers a broader range of housing eras than most of its neighbours, from postwar to current construction.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: A long north-south community with distinct characters at each end: dense and transit-served in the south, closer to conservation land in the north.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Character varies substantially from south to north. Treating Richmond Hill as a single market is a common and expensive mistake.
parks: Richmond Green Sports Centre and Park
landmarks: Richmond Hill Centre for the Performing Arts
transportation: Viva Blue and YRT along Yonge Street
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.

neighbourhoods.name: Whitchurch-Stouffville
neighbourhoods.tagline: Small-town main street, GO line to Union.
neighbourhoods.intro: Whitchurch-Stouffville sits northeast of Markham, keeping a compact main street and a substantial rural land base while the built-up area has grown considerably around the GO corridor.
neighbourhoods.lifestyle: Genuinely small-town in its core, with conservation areas and rural properties within minutes of the main street.
neighbourhoods.housing_note: Rural and acreage properties here involve wells, septic systems and different financing considerations. They are not comparable to serviced-lot suburban homes and should not be priced as though they were.
landmarks: Lebovic Centre for Arts and Entertainment
neighbourhoods.schools_note: Served by the York Region District School Board and York Catholic District School Board. Verify current catchments with the school board.
